title: The Day a Wave of Molasses Hit Boston
script: In 1919, Boston was hit by a tidal wave of molasses. A giant storage tank burst, releasing more than two million gallons of thick, sticky syrup. A wave up to twenty-five feet high tore through the streets at about thirty-five miles an hour. It crushed buildings and trapped people and horses. Twenty-one people died and around one hundred fifty were injured. Locals say on hot days, the neighborhood smelled sweet for decades.
